brief:
The Quincy Institute released an analysis documenting how pro-Israel advocacy groups have influenced American foreign policy decision-making at senior levels of government, the Quincy Institute reported. The investigation examined the revolving door between lobbying organizations and executive and legislative branches, tracking personnel movements and policy outcomes aligned with those groups' priorities.

The institute's findings detail mechanisms through which advocacy organizations have shaped bilateral relations and aid flows. The report examines how staffing patterns and institutional relationships have affected congressional votes and administration positions on Middle East policy. The analysis traces connections between major pro-Israel groups and officials across multiple administrations, mapping the institutional pathways through which lobby priorities reach policymakers.
title: Israel lobby shapes US foreign policy toward Palestine, Quincy Institute reports
